## Construction

Every task is a directory `evals/cases/P9/<case>/` holding a `case.yaml` (the task record: `id`, `property`, `origin`, `grader`, `expect`, `description`, `canary`), a `vuln/` tree with exactly one planted violation, and a `clean/` twin — the same code with the violation fixed through the toolkit primitive. The grader scores both: the violation must be detected in `vuln/` (recall) and not in `clean/` (precision), so the clean twin is the baseline scored alongside every task.

Origins, in the priority order of EVALS-PLAN.md Layer 2:

- **historical-miss** (0): a real miss from this program, encoded permanently.
- **derived** (6): a violation case from the Layer 0 row, in a code shape the historical cases do not already cover.

| task | origin | grader | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `P9-flask-dev-bind-01` | derived | `semgrep` | Flask's development server bound to 0.0.0.0 under __main__, exposing it on every interface. Clean keeps app.run() on 127.0.0.1 for local work; production is served by gunicorn behind the ingress. |
| `P9-flask-dev-bind-02` | derived | `semgrep` | Flask dev server bound to all interfaces via a positional host; clean binds loopback. Sibling shape the rule missed (found by corpus agent A). |
| `P9-torch-load-01` | derived | `semgrep` | torch.load on a downloaded checkpoint without weights_only=True unpickles arbitrary objects (CWE-502). Clean passes weights_only=True. |
| `P9-weak-hash-01` | derived | `semgrep` | hashlib.md5 fingerprints a session token that is later compared to authenticate requests — a security purpose on a broken digest. Clean uses hashlib.sha256. |
| `P9-weak-hash-02` | derived | `semgrep` | hashlib.sha1 as an on-disk cache key — a non-security use that still trips scanners and FIPS builds. Clean keeps the digest and states intent with usedforsecurity=False. |
| `P9-weak-hash-03` | derived | `semgrep` | md5 via hashlib.new for an auth token; clean uses sha256. Sibling shape the rule missed (found by corpus agent A). |

## Metrics and current numbers

- **recall** = tasks whose `vuln/` the grader detected ÷ tasks, Wilson 95% CI.
- **precision** = tasks whose `clean/` the grader did not flag ÷ tasks, Wilson 95% CI.
- with `--trials K > 1`: **pass@k** (any of k) and **pass^k** (all of k) over tasks.

## Known limitations

From the grader docstrings (what each oracle can and cannot decide):

### `semgrep`

> P3/P5/P8/P9 static rules. Detected = `expect.rule` fires in the variant.
>
> Pattern-based: a fix the rule does not recognize is a precision gap (the first
> P8 sink rule flagged `harden()` inline in an f-string), and a vulnerable shape
> the rule has no pattern for is a recall gap — only the shapes in the corpus are
> known covered. Needs the `semgrep` binary; errors (never passes) without it.

## Contamination policy

- **Canary.** Every `case.yaml`, every registry entry and `tasks.jsonl` carry the string in `evals/registry/CANARY.txt` (BIG-bench convention): a model that can reproduce it has seen this corpus in training, and its scores on it do not measure the property.
- **Split.** This eval is `split: build`. Build-split cases are used to tune rules and defenses. The held-out split (`evals/heldout/`, EVALS-PLAN.md Phase 4) is sealed: written after the defenses, never used for tuning, and scored only in reports.
- **No model in the loop.** Every grader is deterministic code; no LLM judges a result, so there is nothing to contaminate on the grading side.
